correctness.rationale: The graph components are directed paths and directed cycles; stable semantics forces a single alternating phase on each path, two phases on each even cycle, none on odd cycles. Thus stable extensions are binary r-vectors, and a pairwise symmetric difference is a weighted Hamming distance with weight ell_i. For any three codewords, a constant column can be changed into a nonconstant column without reducing any distance. Every nonconstant binary triple has exactly one agreeing pair, so assigning each cycle to its agreeing pair gives the pairwise distances W-w_1,W-w_2,W-w_3. Every three-bin assignment is realized by such columns. With r>=2 positive cycles, an optimal partition has max bin weight <W, guaranteeing three distinct codewords. Reachable weighted bin pairs (a,b) give O(rW^2) exact DP. Our independent direct triple-codeword check matched ten multicyclic cases, but the column partition argument is the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The simultaneous three-extension diversity objective is natural for selecting genuinely different explanations in argumentation semantics. The theorem gives an exact all-instance answer and polynomial-time algorithm for a structural graph fragment that can have exponentially many extensions, with a sharp balance criterion.

final_claim: For finite attack graphs with indegree and outdegree <=1, with r>=2 even directed cycles of lengths ell_i and no odd directed cycle, the max-min symmetric-difference diversity of three distinct stable extensions equals W minus optimal three-bin makespan of ell_i, with W=sum ell_i; a DP computes it in O(r W^2) time, and the equality threshold 2W/3 occurs precisely with three equal total bin weights.
limitations: An earlier exact three-codeword packing formula in weighted binary Hamming space may imply this specialization.
The claim excludes branching graphs, odd cycles and cases with fewer than three stable extensions.
